title: Do we all see the same colour
titleChinese: 每个人看到的颜色都一样吗？
paragraphs: Have you ever wondered if you see the same colours as other people? Most people know what blue is when they see it. It’s the colour of sea, sky and sapphires. They see the colour and call it ‘blue’ because they were taught the word and associated it with what they saw. But how do you know what you see as blue isn’t someone else’s red, and vice versa?

The ability to perceive different colours is down to receptors in our eyes known as cones. Light waves hit these receptors and they react depending on which colour the light is, sending signals to the brain. The brain then decodes these signals to determine which colour light the eyes are receiving.

Some people’s receptors are more developed than others. People with weaker receptors usually have colour blindness. The inability of the receptor to interpret the light waves correctly means that some people cannot distinguish between different shades of a colour.

Those with more enhanced receptors can see more shades of one colour, which is the first way in which people may see colours differently from each other. We sometimes hear people having an argument about whether something is dark blue or black. It might be because one person has stronger receptors to interpret the light than another.

In the past, most scientists would argue that everyone saw colours in the same way. However, research was conducted on monkeys, in which they were injected with a virus affecting their receptors. This enabled them to distinguish more colours than usual and brought an intriguing revelation. Normally monkeys can only see in blue and green, but the virus allowed monkeys to see red.

The neurons in their brains spontaneously adapted to be able to understand new colours, which might mean the neurons in our brains are not hardwired to automatically understand which colour is which. This implies that our brains and neurons may adapt depending on our stimulus during the developmental phase. Colour could be a very personal experience, unique to everyone.

So, the next time you talk about your favourite colour, just remember if yours is blue and your friend says red, you might actually be thinking about the same colour. What if everyone in the world has the same favourite colour, but just calls it different names?

vocabulary.entry: sapphire /ˈsæfaɪə(r)/ n. 蓝宝石
vocabulary.example: She wore a bracelet studded with small sapphires.
vocabulary.translation: 她戴了一只镶嵌着小蓝宝石的手镯。

vocabulary.entry: associate /əˈsəʊʃieɪt/ v. 把……联系在一起；联想
vocabulary.example: People often associate the smell of baking with their childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 人们常常把烘焙的香味和童年联系在一起。

vocabulary.entry: vice versa /ˌvaɪs ˈvɜːsə/ 反之亦然（俗语）
vocabulary.example: I respect her and vice versa.
vocabulary.translation: 我尊重她，她也尊重我。

vocabulary.entry: perceive /pəˈsiːv/ v. 感知；察觉；意识到
vocabulary.example: We perceive colours with the receptors in our eyes.
vocabulary.translation: 我们靠眼睛里的感受器感知颜色。

vocabulary.entry: receptor /rɪˈseptə(r)/ n. 感受器；受体
vocabulary.example: The drug binds to specific receptors in the brain.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药物会与大脑中的特定受体相结合。

vocabulary.entry: cone /kəʊn/ n. （眼睛的）视锥细胞
vocabulary.example: Cones in the retina are responsible for colour vision.
vocabulary.translation: 视网膜中的视锥细胞负责色彩视觉。

vocabulary.entry: light wave /laɪt weɪv/ n. 光波
vocabulary.example: Light waves travel at a speed of about 300,000 kilometres per second.
vocabulary.translation: 光波的传播速度约为每秒30万公里。

vocabulary.entry: decode /ˌdiːˈkəʊd/ v. 解码；破译
vocabulary.example: The computer can decode the encrypted data quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 这台电脑能快速破译加密数据。

vocabulary.entry: colour blindness /ˈkʌlə ˈblaɪndnəs/ n. 色盲
vocabulary.example: He has a mild form of colour blindness and can't tell red from green.
vocabulary.translation: 他患有轻度色盲，无法区分红色和绿色。

vocabulary.entry: interpret /ɪnˈtɜːprɪt/ v. 解读；阐释；理解
vocabulary.example: The audience interpreted the actor's smile as a sign of confidence.
vocabulary.translation: 观众把这位演员的微笑解读为自信的表现。

vocabulary.entry: distinguish /dɪˈstɪŋɡwɪʃ/ v. 区分；辨别；分清
vocabulary.example: It's hard to distinguish the two species of birds.
vocabulary.translation: 很难区分这两种鸟类。

vocabulary.entry: shade /ʃeɪd/ n. 色调；浓淡；色度
vocabulary.example: This paint is available in several different shades of blue.
vocabulary.translation: 这种颜料有好几种不同深浅的蓝色色调。

vocabulary.entry: enhanced /ɪnˈhɑːnst/ adj. 增强的；提高的；改进的
vocabulary.example: The device has an enhanced camera with better low-light performance.
vocabulary.translation: 这款设备配备了增强型摄像头，弱光拍摄效果更佳。

vocabulary.entry: inject /ɪnˈdʒekt/ v. 注射；注入
vocabulary.example: The doctor injected the vaccine into my arm.
vocabulary.translation: 医生把疫苗注射到了我的胳膊里。

vocabulary.entry: intriguing /ɪnˈtriːɡɪŋ/ adj. 非常有趣的；引人入胜的；神秘的
vocabulary.example: The book tells an intriguing story about ancient civilizations.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书讲述了一个关于古代文明的引人入胜的故事。

vocabulary.entry: revelation /ˌrevəˈleɪʃn/ n. 揭示；透露；新发现
vocabulary.example: The investigation led to a startling revelation about the company's finances.
vocabulary.translation: 这次调查揭露了一个关于该公司财务状况的惊人真相。

vocabulary.entry: neuron /ˈnjʊərɒn/ n. 神经元；神经细胞
vocabulary.example: Neurons transmit information throughout the nervous system.
vocabulary.translation: 神经元在整个神经系统中传递信息。

vocabulary.entry: spontaneously /spɒnˈteɪniəsli/ adv. 自发地；不由自主地
vocabulary.example: The crowd spontaneously broke into applause.
vocabulary.translation: 人群自发地鼓起掌来。

vocabulary.entry: adapt /əˈdæpt/ v. 适应；调整
vocabulary.example: Animals need to adapt to changing environmental conditions.
vocabulary.translation: 动物需要适应不断变化的环境条件。

vocabulary.entry: hardwired /ˈhɑːdwaɪəd/ adj. （计算机系统或大脑）天生的；固有的
vocabulary.example: Some people believe that empathy is hardwired into human beings.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人认为共情能力是人类与生俱来的。

vocabulary.entry: stimulus /ˈstɪmjələs/ n. 刺激物；促进因素
vocabulary.example: The sound of a bell is a stimulus that makes the dog salivate.
vocabulary.translation: 铃声是一种能让狗分泌唾液的刺激物。

vocabulary.entry: developmental phase /dɪˌveləpˈmentl feɪz/ n. 发育阶段；发展阶段
vocabulary.example: Children go through several important developmental phases in their first five years.
vocabulary.translation: 儿童在五岁前会经历几个重要的发育阶段。

sentences.english: Have you ever wondered if you see the same colours as other people?
sentences.chinese: 你是否曾好奇过，自己看到的颜色和别人看到的是不是一样的？

sentences.chinese: 大多数人看到蓝色时都能认出来，它是大海、天空和蓝宝石的颜色。

sentences.chinese: 但你怎么知道，自己眼中的蓝色，不会是别人眼中的红色呢？

sentences.english: But how do you know what you see as blue isn’t someone else’s red, and vice versa?
sentences.chinese: 反之亦然。

sentences.chinese: 感知不同颜色的能力，取决于我们眼睛里一种叫做视锥细胞的感受器。

sentences.chinese: 光波照射到这些感受器上时，感受器会根据光的颜色产生不同反应，并向大脑发送信号。

sentences.english: The brain then decodes these signals to determine which colour light the eyes are receiving.
sentences.chinese: 随后大脑会解码这些信号，从而判断眼睛接收到的光是什么颜色。

sentences.english: Some people’s receptors are more developed than others.
sentences.chinese: 有些人的感受器发育得比其他人更好。

sentences.english: People with weaker receptors usually have colour blindness.
sentences.chinese: 感受器功能较弱的人通常会患有色盲。

sentences.english: The inability of the receptor to interpret the light waves correctly means that some people cannot distinguish between different shades of a colour.
sentences.chinese: 感受器无法正确解读光波，就意味着这些人无法区分同一种颜色的不同深浅色调。

sentences.english: Those with more enhanced receptors can see more shades of one colour, which is the first way in which people may see colours differently from each other.
sentences.chinese: 感受器功能更强的人，能看到同一种颜色更多的色调变化，这是人与人之间颜色感知存在差异的第一个原因。

sentences.english: We sometimes hear people having an argument about whether something is dark blue or black. It might be because one person has stronger receptors to interpret the light than another.
sentences.chinese: 我们有时会听到人们争论某样东西到底是深蓝色还是黑色，这很可能是因为其中一个人解读光线的感受器功能比另一个人更强。

sentences.english: In the past, most scientists would argue that everyone saw colours in the same way.
sentences.chinese: 过去，大多数科学家都认为，所有人看到的颜色都是一样的。

sentences.english: However, research was conducted on monkeys, in which they were injected with a virus affecting their receptors. This enabled them to distinguish more colours than usual and brought an intriguing revelation.
sentences.chinese: 然而，一项针对猴子的研究得出了一个有趣的新发现——研究人员给猴子注射了一种会影响其感受器的病毒，让它们能比平时分辨出更多颜色。

sentences.english: Normally monkeys can only see in blue and green, but the virus allowed monkeys to see red.
sentences.chinese: 通常情况下，猴子只能看到蓝色和绿色，而这种病毒让它们看到了红色。

sentences.chinese: 这表明，在发育阶段，我们的大脑和神经元可能会根据外界刺激发生适应性变化。

sentences.chinese: 因此，颜色感知可能是一种非常个人化的体验，因人而异，独一无二。

sentences.english: So, the next time you talk about your favourite colour, just remember if yours is blue and your friend says red, you might actually be thinking about the same colour.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次你和别人聊起自己最喜欢的颜色时，不妨想一想：如果你喜欢的是蓝色，而你的朋友喜欢的是红色，你们俩说的也许其实是同一种颜色。

sentences.english: What if everyone in the world has the same favourite colour, but just calls it different names?
sentences.chinese: 要是全世界的人最喜欢的都是同一种颜色，只是叫法不同，那会怎么样呢？
